title: Harbor: inventory handoff training
description: A fictional sample presentation for evaluating complete-clip selection and matched delivery. All scenarios and outcomes are invented.

segments.title: Start the next shift with the facts
segments.transcript: Welcome to Harbor, a fictional training concept for inventory handoffs. At the end of a shift, the incoming team needs to know what was counted, which items still need checking, and who owns each open question. This short example introduces a shared handoff record.
segments.slide_text:
Harbor
What was counted?
What needs checking?
Who owns the next check?

segments.title: One invented stockroom
segments.transcript: This example uses one invented stockroom and ten simulated handoffs. Every count and outcome is made up for training. The finding that follows applies only to this fictional setting.
segments.slide_text:
10 simulated handoffs
One invented stockroom
Illustrative counts only

segments.title: An illustrative finding
segments.transcript: In the fictional exercise, three unassigned stock questions became one after the handoff record was completed. This is an illustrative finding. Keep its setting.
segments.slide_text:
Unassigned stock questions
3 before; 1 after
Only in the fictional setting

segments.title: Record the count and the open question
segments.transcript: To use the proposed record, enter the item, the counted quantity, and the location checked. Add any unresolved question and name the person who will check it next. The incoming shift reads the open items before accepting the handoff. If a count looks wrong, keep the uncertainty visible and ask for another check.
segments.slide_text:
Item, quantity, location
Open question and owner
Read before accepting
